publisher: Center for Strategic and International Studies
title: New Executive Order Ties U.S. Critical Minerals Security to Global Partnerships
key_claim: On 15 January 2026 President Trump signed an executive order, Adjusting Imports of Processed Critical Minerals and Their Derivative Products into the United States, which recognises price volatility in critical mineral markets as a structural national security vulnerability that undermines private investment and discourages market-based economies from sustaining capacity, and directs the secretary of commerce and the US trade representative to consider price support mechanisms - such as price floors - within negotiated trade agreements; the EO frames critical minerals as foundational inputs across all 16 critical infrastructure sectors and the defense industrial base, and the US is fully import-dependent for 12 critical minerals and reliant on imports for more than half of consumption of an additional 29, while China produces only ~10% of global lithium, cobalt and copper yet controls 40-90% of world processing capacity for these materials.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank analysis by the Director of CSIS Critical Minerals Security Program. Structural anchor (3-6m band): the canonical interpretation of the 15 January 2026 Executive Order.

title: Lender to Market Maker: The New U.S. Government Critical Minerals Playbook
date_evidence: February 13, 2026 ... Christopher R. LeWand, Global Practice Leader Power, Renewables & Energy Transition (PRET)
key_claim: The US Government has shifted from de-risking projects to actively shaping markets via a multi-instrument playbook: federal loans and export credit, equity and quasi-equity stakes (the July 2025 DoD-MP Materials partnership combined ~15% US Government equity, a $150M loan and 10-year floor-price and offtake commitments), and supply- and demand-side market-making (offtake, strategic stockpiles, and price floors, including a January 2026 bipartisan $2.5bn Strategic Resilience Reserve designed to pay above prevailing market prices to anchor a Western benchmark); the Office of Strategic Capital's mandate expanded from ~$1bn to $200bn. The article names three risks: market distortion (price floors and stockpiles may dampen market signals or entrench higher costs); governance complexity; and execution risk (permitting, construction, technology scale-up).
notes: Tier 2 consultancy article. Anchors the full federal toolkit and supplies the self-disclosed risks that serve as the counter-argument's policy critique.

title: Special Report 04/2026 - Critical raw materials for the energy transition: Not a rock-solid policy
date_evidence: Released on 2 February 2026, the ECA report ... Special Report 04/2026, 'Critical raw materials for the energy transition - Not a rock-solid policy'
key_claim: The European Court of Auditors Special Report 04/2026 (published 2 February 2026) finds the EU's 2030 targets under the 2024 Critical Raw Materials Act - 10% local extraction, 40% EU processing and 25% recycled content - appear out of reach: diversification of suppliers is not producing tangible results (between 2020 and 2024 imports from partner countries decreased for about half of the materials examined); new EU mining projects can take up to 20 years to become operational; 7 of 26 strategic materials have recycling rates of 1-5% and 10 are not recycled at all; 7 of the EU's 14 strategic raw materials partnerships are with countries of limited political and economic stability.
notes: Tier 1 EU institutional auditor. Anchors the EU side: diversification-led strategy is not delivering, sharpening why the US has shifted to price-floor mechanics.

title: Rare earths surge above price floor given to MP Materials
date_evidence: Rare earths surge above price floor given to MP Materials. The article was published on February 18, 2026, by Reuters. ... rally in prices to $123 a kg, the highest since July 2022 ... above the threshold of $110 per kg.
key_claim: Prices of neodymium and praseodymium (NdPr) rallied above the US government's $110/kg price floor for MP Materials in mid-February 2026, reaching ~$123/kg - the highest since July 2022 - meaning the US will not have to subsidise MP Materials' output as long as prices remain above the threshold. China dominates the global supply chain, accounting for 90% of refining capacity and around 70% of mined output.
notes: Tier 3 Reuters wire syndicated by Mining.com. Used for the concrete data point that the floor mechanism is in operation and prices spiked above it.

title: Column: West needs its own pricing to escape China's rare earths grip
key_claim: The US-DoD/MP Materials price-floor deal currently uses Asian Metal's ex-works China NdPr index as its reference price; both Asian Metal and Shanghai Metal Market operate within Beijing's 1998 Pricing Law, which a November 2025 US Select Committee on China report states 'effectively makes it illegal to publish prices that deviate from the PRC government's wishes'; the deal has an escape clause to switch to a non-China benchmark if one emerges; Benchmark Mineral Intelligence has started collecting non-China rare-earth prices, CME and ICE are studying rare-earth futures contracts, and CME lithium-hydroxide contract volumes grew 37% year-on-year in 2025. Conclusion: even with US price floors, the West remains tied to Chinese price discovery until a Western pricing infrastructure is built.
notes: Tier 3 Reuters column. Surfaces the key nuance: the floor sits on top of Chinese price discovery, and the deeper signal is Western pricing architecture.

title: The Critical Minerals Report (02.22.2026): The Price-Floor Era Arrives for Rare Earths and Uranium
key_claim: By late February 2026 the price-floor era has arrived: NdPr surged above the $110/kg MP Materials floor (Reuters, 18 February); US agencies have developed a broader critical-minerals price floor system, now being discussed with allies (Bloomberg, 17 February); the US Department of Commerce final determination in the Chinese graphite anti-dumping investigation (17 February) could lift total US duties on certain Chinese battery-grade graphite to approximately 220%; the US-Uzbekistan critical minerals pact (18 February) and the US-Japan $36bn slate of energy and critical minerals projects extend the architecture into a network of bilateral agreements; the European Court of Auditors reports the EU's 2030 Critical Raw Materials Act targets appear out of reach.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press (Critical Minerals Institute weekly report). Aggregates the cluster of February 2026 developments that constitute the 'price-floor era' arrival.

title: Lynas-Japan deal offers 'insulation' from China rare earth pricing
key_claim: A revised offtake agreement signed in March 2026 commits JARE (Japan Australia Rare Earths) to buy 5,000 tonnes of NdPr annually from Lynas Rare Earths at a $110/kg floor price until 2038, plus 50% of Lynas's heavy rare earths (dysprosium and terbium); the $110/kg floor mirrors the MP Materials-DoD floor, establishing a consensus NdPr price floor for Western supply chains; the revised offtake provides insulation from Chinese rare-earth pricing, replacing the 2011 offtake that was linked to Chinese benchmarks; Lynas shares jumped 16% to A$20.59. Japan's reliance on Chinese rare earths has dropped from 90% in 2010 to 60-70% today.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press. The material extension of the US $110/kg floor into a private allied offtake. Key in-window evidence.

title: The Critical Minerals Report (03.15.2026): Price Floors Arrive, Lynas-Japan Deal Reshapes Rare Earth Markets and U.S. DoD Solicits Supply of 13 Critical Minerals
date_evidence: Tracy Hughes. March 15, 2026. ... the center of gravity in critical minerals shifted from 'find more supply' to 'design a market that can finance it.'
key_claim: By mid-March 2026 the US Trade Representative has opened a public consultation on a plurilateral trade architecture asking industry how minimum prices, reference prices and border measures could be engineered to stabilise investment returns in critical minerals, with the consultation closing March 19 and negotiations with the EU and Japan targeted for April; the Lynas-JARE $110/kg NdPr floor through 2038 is the first commercial contracting to mirror the US price-floor policy; the Pentagon solicited supply for 13 critical minerals (proposal deadline March 20); Canada announced 30 new critical minerals partnerships unlocking C$12.1bn; UN political leadership warns demand for technology minerals could triple by 2030 and quadruple by 2040; critical-minerals policy is increasingly being written as market structure, not merely as subsidy.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press (Critical Minerals Institute weekly report). In-window. Anchors the USTR plurilateral consultation framing and the multilateralisation of the $110/kg architecture.
